A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BWCache and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The shared method and experiments can be matched reliably despite added material, renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation quality, latency, multi-GPU scaling and ablation results on Open-Sora, Open-Sora-Plan and Latte, including statistical comparisons in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on Wan 2.1 and HunyuanVideo, additional comparators, memory measurements and feature-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: v1 computes the similarity indicator across all blocks. v3 Appendix D.5 introduces an adaptation using uniformly spaced subsets, defaulting to 50% of blocks for Wan 2.1 and HunyuanVideo. The threshold trigger, final-step recomputation and periodic reuse procedure remain unchanged. Pooling and compression are suggested options rather than demonstrated additions.

E1.justification: The main video-generation task and prompt sources remain Open-Sora gallery, VBench and T2V-CompBench. v3 Appendix E.2 adds limited diagnostic coverage of text-to-image and class-conditional generation. The high-motion evaluation selects from already represented videos; adding video backbones alone does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds FasterCache on all three original backbones and Skip-DiT on Latte. Appendix D.1 evaluates ProfilingDiT and TaylorSeer against BWCache on shortened Wan 2.1 and HunyuanVideo sequences. Table 2 also adds TeaCache to the existing multi-GPU comparisons, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds FlowMatch-based backbone configurations, 9-frame and 17-frame comparisons accommodating baseline memory limits, block-fraction sweeps, and memory and indicator-time measurements. FLOPs are removed from the evaluation metrics. Figure 7 replaces several original Open-Sora resolution/length configurations with Open-Sora-Plan and Wan configurations. The original models' schedules and default threshold/reuse interval remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-model feature trajectories, block-versus-timestep feature comparisons, memory/OOM analysis, indicator-overhead measurements, block-fraction sensitivity, high-motion evaluation and latent-drift analysis. These substantially extend the questions investigated. The reduced-inference-step comparison already appeared in v1 Appendix C.3 and is relocated to Section 4.4; existing reuse-interval and final-step ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Table 9 and v3 Table 10 use the same paired t-tests, means, standard deviations, p-values and confidence intervals. v3 extends this reporting to additional model rows without changing the statistical procedure. Neither version supplies changed repeated-run counts or seed information.

E6.justification: The shared Table 1 scores for the original three backbones remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for new comparators, backbones and supplementary analyses. Newly reported BWCache results include 81.99% VBench with 2.00× speedup on Wan 2.1 and 82.48% with 2.60× on HunyuanVideo; these are new-setting results, not matched-run gains. FLOPs entries and several Open-Sora scaling configurations are removed.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11) retain the diffusion formulation, block operations, relative-L1 definitions, caching criterion, reuse schedule and metric formulas, with notation changes only. The added frequency-domain and noise-schedule explanations are conceptual interpretations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains training-free block-wise caching with similarity-based decisions and periodic recomputation. The abstract increases the reported maximum speedup from 2.24× to 2.6×, and the introduction adds explicit memory-efficiency positioning. These refine the performance and practicality claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds frequency/noise-schedule explanations for feature trajectories, a prompt-adaptivity explanation for block-level caching, and substantive discussion of memory constraints. Appendix E distinguishes image/class-conditional feature patterns from the video U-shape and explains why latent drift cannot be controlled through L1 monitoring alone. These materially expand mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 adds scheduler/encoder settings for the new backbones, explicit ProfilingDiT and TaylorSeer parameters, uniformly spaced block-selection details, NVLink information and model-specific threshold guidance. The existing hardware/software disclosures, default threshold and reuse interval, and code-access link remain unchanged. These are useful additions rather than a comprehensive reproducibility overhaul.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against closely related caching methods: it distinguishes BWCache from Skip-DiT's architectural changes/retraining and ProfilingDiT/TaylorSeer's feature-storage demands. It also introduces cited frequency-domain and noise-schedule explanations. FasterCache was already cited in v1; its publication update alone is not new related work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Targeted edits clarify terminology, move the reduced-step experiment from the appendix into Section 4.4, and organize added material into feature-reuse and discussion appendices. Acknowledgements, an LLM-use statement and conference-header/affiliation edits are added; the original narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the caching overview, adds a model diagram, reorganizes and expands the qualitative comparison grid, changes scaling-plot panels, and adds multiple feature-analysis and resource tables/figures. Table 1 gains comparison rows and loses its FLOPs column. Existing reduced-step displays move into the main text, and the document adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v1 established quality/latency benefits but did not quantify memory or indicator overhead and lacked several relevant evaluated comparators. v3's expanded comparisons and Appendices D–E substantially strengthen evidence about practical costs, motion sensitivity and applicability limits. These address important weaknesses in an inference-acceleration paper. Dropped FLOPs reporting and some overbroad summaries remain drawbacks—for example, Section 4.3 claims superiority over TeaCache despite its lower Open-Sora-Plan latencies in Table 2—but do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
